function.arguments: {"observation": "`patient_id` has 48 duplicate values — rows may not be one-per-entity", "implication": "The `patient_id` column is not unique across rows, which means some patients appear more than once in the dataset. This violates the assumption of one row per patient, which is critical for computing population-level means. If we compute the mean without deduplicating, we will double-count (or more) some patients, leading to biased results. The data dictionary states that `sample_seq` indicates assay run number and that the row with the highest `sample_seq` supersedes earlier rows for the same patient. Therefore, we must deduplicate the dataset on `patient_id`, keeping only the row with the highest `sample_seq` per patient. This ensures one row per patient, which is required by the population definition in the contract ('all patients in the trial, with one row per patient')."}
function.name: note_finding
